issues.description: The Windows bootstrap silently falls back to legacy Windows PowerShell even though that shell has a known module-loading failure for the installer command, leaving users without actionable guidance to use pwsh.
issues.rationale: At the selected pre-comment head, `get_powershell_command` returns `powershell` whenever its `/ ?`-style availability probe succeeds, without telling the user that this is legacy Windows PowerShell 5.x or that the later installer command can abort while loading `Microsoft.PowerShell.Security`. Collaborator comment 3121739038 reports that concrete failure and requests a warning recommending PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`). Commit ef0cb9fd2aecf00afd1e4c8ac08980e1bb092710 adds exactly that warning before returning the fallback, and the reviewer then approves the change. The failure condition is Windows without working `pwsh`, with `powershell` installed but unable to execute the installer because `Get-ExecutionPolicy`'s module cannot load.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Windows bootstrap and Verus were not executed. Selected the latest PR head before issue comment 3121739038 by commit/comment chronology, confirmed its official merge-base, and compared repair commit ef0cb9fd2aecf00afd1e4c8ac08980e1bb092710 plus the final reviewer approval.
